suez_20_day_detour.price_summary: For a 4.31% supply loss the linear formula implies about a +28.8% price move (supply loss divided by 0.15), held for 60 days and then decaying toward baseline with a 30-day half-life. The shaded band is plus or minus 13.09 percentage points, the formula's average error across 21 historical events.
suez_20_day_detour.price_takeaway: The linear formula implies a peak of +28.8%, with a ±13.09 pp band.
price_assumptions: %dP = %dS / |Ed|, Ed = -0.15 (borrowed textbook short-run value). Phase 1 tested a trained model on 21 events and it did not beat this formula.
Band of ±13.09 pp = leave-one-out mean absolute error of the formula on 21 daily-resolution events, all with supply loss up to 8% (small sample). It does not apply beyond that.
Exponential decay after the disruption with a 30-day half-life (default: half the duration, clamped to 7 to 60 days).
Price is assumed to move linearly with supply loss; this is unverified for very large shocks and no nonlinear model or cap is applied.

hormuz_blockade.price_summary: For a 15.49% supply loss the linear formula implies about a +103.3% price move (supply loss divided by 0.15), held for 30 days and then decaying toward baseline with a 15-day half-life. This is outside the validated range: the largest validated event, 2026 US-Israel War on Iran (Hormuz Blockade), had a supply loss of 8% and an actual price move of +57.8%, and the plus or minus 13.09 percentage point error band, measured only on events up to 8% supply loss, is not validated at this magnitude and is not shown. The blockade result depends on the bypass assumption: with the headline 4.7 million barrels per day of pipeline bypass the price impact is +103.3%, with the lower 2.6 million case it is +116.8%.
hormuz_blockade.price_takeaway: The linear formula implies a peak of +103.3%, outside the validated range (largest validated event: +57.8% at 8% supply loss).
price_assumptions: %dP = %dS / |Ed|, Ed = -0.15 (borrowed textbook short-run value). Phase 1 tested a trained model on 21 events and it did not beat this formula.
Band of ±13.09 pp = leave-one-out mean absolute error of the formula on 21 daily-resolution events, all with supply loss up to 8% (small sample). It does not apply beyond that.
Exponential decay after the disruption with a 15-day half-life (default: half the duration, clamped to 7 to 60 days).
Price is assumed to move linearly with supply loss; this is unverified for very large shocks and no nonlinear model or cap is applied.
